page: Amazon Web Services r5ad.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a single physical AMD EPYC 7571 processor core providing two dedicated vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading at a 2.2 GHz base clock. The configuration supplies 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached directly to the instance is 75 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are included in this instance type.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest compute capacity consistent with its entry-level two-vCPU sizing and first-generation EPYC architecture. Compute-focused metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 711.0, a multi-core score of 948.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 1886.24, place overall CPU processing in the lower performance tiers. Read memory bandwidth achieves 22.2 GB/sec on uncached large blocks, while write throughput measures 12.61 GB/sec. Instruction support encompasses AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, but excludes newer instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX.

The inclusion of 75 GB of direct NVMe ephemeral storage provides fast local scratch space, complementing operations like the 1.26 million operations per second recorded in Redis SET workloads. However, the trade-off remains moderate raw processing power and baseline 1 Gbps networking. As a result, the r5ad.large serves effectively for cost-conscious, memory-dependent small workloads such as caching layers, development databases, and moderate memory-buffered services rather than compute-heavy batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r5ad.large is a memory-optimized Nitro hypervisor instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core, 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM (8.0 GB per vCPU), and a bundled 75 GB local NVMe SSD storage volume. Network connectivity provides a baseline speed of 1 Gbps, with zero GPUs included. Across synthetic benchmarks, the instance yields entry-level compute throughput, recording 711.0 in Geekbench single-core, 948.0 in multi-core, and 1.26 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. Its generous RAM-to-CPU ratio and low-latency NVMe scratch disk make the r5ad.large well-suited for lightweight in-memory caching, temporary scratchpad storage, and small database deployments.
